findings.conclusion: Multiple complete portal proposals improve this development cohort over first-feasible routing, at substantial CPU search work. They do not close the flat-baseline PIP gap or physical QoR gate.

limitations: Single fixed 70-net development cohort; no held-out generalization claim.
Upstream portal choices are greedy. Candidate/attempt limits do not enumerate all multi-hop corridors.
Per-invocation best incremental cost does not guarantee the smallest eventual shared tree.
PIP count is not physical wirelength; algorithm cost is not delay; concurrent-run counters are not latency.
Changed trees have no new DCP connectivity, native DRC/STA, bus-skew or bitstream signoff.
Serial candidate-local reservations and source-observer shadows are not distributed capacity grants or partitioned hardware authority.
next_work: Develop reachability/cost-aware portal proposals or a monotone-die oracle to separate candidate coverage from die-constrained path cost.
Reduce repeated local searches and heuristic preparation while preserving the full cost/authority protocol.
Complete native physical QoR, representative held-out cohorts, die-local/HBM implementation, full ablations, board validation and paper.
